transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-08-03 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (HelixBridge Head of Infrastructure), Anika Bose (Security Lead), Devon Grant (Platform Engineer)

Summary:
High-level discovery about private/VPC deployment for Redwood Private. Focus areas: private dataplane topology, namespace routing (how to isolate model tenants), egress controls for regulated APAC region, KMS/HSM and audit log needs, and pilot scope.

Topics:
- VPC peering vs Transit Gateway vs PrivateLink
- Private endpoints and cross-account access patterns
- IP planning, NAT concurrency, and egress bandwidth for inference traffic
- Region constraints (APAC data residency + eu-west fallback)
- Security: SOC2, KMS, customer-managed keys, audit trails

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: okay hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate it. quick intros, I'm Liam, AE on the Redwood inference team.
[00:07] Marco Ruiz: yeah thanks, Marco here, head of infra at HelixBridge. we run a multiregional platform, mostly GCP and AWS, and we're looking at private inference options.
[00:14] Anika Bose: Anika, security, i'll be focused on kms, audit, and residency.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood engineering, i'll cover the topology and latency constraints.
[00:22] Devon Grant: Devon, platform eng, i'll be hands on if we move to pilot.
[00:25] Liam Chen: awesome, we'll go through a quick discovery. Marco, what's driving this now—are you evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private, or is private the only option?
[00:34] Marco Ruiz: Private is preferred. we have data residency in APAC for one vertical, and certain PII cannot touch public endpoints. also cost predictability for our inference pipelines is important.
[00:44] Priya Nair: got it. when you say private, do you mean VPC peering into our vpc, classic peer-to-peer, or a private endpoint/service endpoint model where connections are initiated outbound from your VPC?
[00:56] Marco Ruiz: good question. we were thinking Transit Gateway on AWS for central routing, but we also have cross-account constraints—some of our teams run in a different account.
[01:05] Devon Grant: to add, latency matters—sub-100ms 99th maybe for our synchronous features. but a lot of batch inference can tolerate higher. the big thing is egress: how do we control where traffic goes, and ensure logs/audits stay within region.
[01:18] Priya Nair: okay so two axis: control plane vs dataplane. Redwood Private can run a control plane in your VPC or in a Redwood-managed control plane with private connectivity. for dataplane, we support private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink style), or peering/transit setups. PrivateLink gives you cross-account private access without exposing public IPs.
[01:35] Anika Bose: does PrivateLink support cross-region? we need APAC region run and a failover to eu-west but can't replicate PII outside the APAC region for primary processing.
[01:43] Priya Nair: PrivateLink is regional; for cross-region you'd typically have endpoints in each region and route requests accordingly. for failover we can configure routing policies to prefer APAC endpoints and failover to eu-west if capacity issues—however you'd need to consider data residency for hot data.
[01:56] Marco Ruiz: that makes sense. what about Transit Gateway? we already use TGW for some services. would Redwood sit behind our TGW?
[02:04] Priya Nair: yes, we can attach to TGW. common pattern is: create a dedicated Redwood VPC per region, peer it to your TGW, then use route tables to control which subnets can reach the inference nodes. disadvantage is more IP space planning and potential route table churn.
[02:18] Liam Chen: and just to be clear, Readwood—sorry Redwood—offers a private deployment package where the inference nodes run in your cloud account (customer-managed) or in our dedicated account with strict peering. Priya, you want to explain shared vs customer-managed?
[02:30] Priya Nair: yeah. customer-managed means all compute (GPU nodes) live in your accounts, you control networking/KMS. shared/dedicated means Redwood provisions the infra but uses VPC peering or PrivateLink to provide logical isolation. customer-managed gives maximum isolation and KMS control but takes longer to onboard.
[02:46] Marco Ruiz: leaning customer-managed. we must hold keys in our HSM for certain models. is there an HSM/KMS integration?
[02:52] Priya Nair: yes we integrate with customer KMS/HSM systems, we can reference keys for model encryption and for audit signing. note: some of the model runtime components require plaintext model weights in memory, so the key is about at-rest and transit encryption and audit, not eliminating in-memory plaintext.
[03:08] Anika Bose: that's ok, we had expected that. audit logs—can we get token-level logs and request tracing into our centralized SIEM?
[03:15] Priya Nair: yes, we can stream audit logs (structured) into your logging endpoints—CloudWatch, Stackdriver, or a log collector via private egress. we also support audit log retention policies.
[03:24] Devon Grant: quick question on IPs and NAT. If we run customer-managed in our account, do we NAT outbound to public internet for model downloads/updates and for telemetry to Redwood control plane?
[03:35] Priya Nair: model downloads can be staged—either you pull them into your private storage (recommended) or we pull them via signed access over an egress path. For telemetry/control-plane comms, you can route it through private endpoints back to Redwood control plane, or allow egress with strict whitelisting.
[03:49] Marco Ruiz: if we want no public egress, what's the pattern?
[03:52] Priya Nair: typically you set up PrivateLink endpoints for the control plane APIs, and use S3 VPC endpoints or GCS private access for model blobs. then no public internet egress needed. but that requires VPC endpoints in region and appropriate IAM roles.
[04:04] Liam Chen: also note that some customers prefer a hybrid: control plane in Redwood but data plane in customer account, and a periodic pull of model updates via a signed S3 bucket.
[04:13] Marco Ruiz: ok. latency question—what's the typical tail latency impact for PrivateLink vs peering?
[04:18] Priya Nair: PrivateLink adds a small proxy hop but is generally comparable to peering; peering with TGW can be lower latency but more brittle with route convergence. for strict SLOs we recommend colocating the dataplane in the same region and AZs.
[04:32] Devon Grant: and concurrency? how many open connections/persistent sockets per instance? we use massive concurrent websockets right now.
[04:40] Priya Nair: our runtime supports thousands of concurrent sessions per GPU node depending on model size and batching. there are limits at NAT gateways and LB levels; if you're using NAT GW we need to plan for SNAT exhaustion, so we recommend using private endpoints or allocating enough NAT IPs.
[04:56] Anika Bose: SNAT exhaustion has bitten us before. would Redwood recommend using NLB with IP target mode or something?
[05:02] Priya Nair: yes, NLB with private IP targets or endpoint services are common patterns to avoid SNAT issues. also consider AWS 'Gateway Load Balancer' in some architectures.
[05:09] Marco Ruiz: sounds good. what about cost? we're evaluating Dedicated as well for predictability. Redwood, how do you price private customer-managed infra vs dedicated reserved?
[05:18] Liam Chen: pricing can be capacity-based for Dedicated (monthly commit) and for customer-managed typically we have a managed-license plus per-instance runtime fee. we'll follow up with a pricing sheet tailored to your expected QPS and model sizes.
[05:31] Devon Grant: security review: do you have SOC2 and pen test reports?
[05:34] Liam Chen: yes SOC2 Type II, and periodic pen testing—Priya will share the security pack. sometimes the pdfs get garbled in transcription, but we'll attach them to the CRM.
[05:42] Anika Bose: we also need SSO/SAML integration and RBAC—can you integrate with our IdP for tenant isolation?
[05:48] Priya Nair: yes SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported, plus RBAC scopes for tenant-level access. for audit we can attribute requests to IdP identities.
[05:56] Marco Ruiz: network peering with multiple accounts—how do you handle prefix overlapping?
[06:01] Priya Nair: we request unique CIDR blocks for Redwood subnets and ask customers to avoid overlap. if overlap exists, we can use NAT-translated jump boxes but it's messy. best to reserve a pair of /20s per region.
[06:13] Devon Grant: do you have a recommended IP plan doc?
[06:16] Priya Nair: yes we'll send an IP planning template.
[06:19] Liam Chen: noted in action items.
[06:22] Marco Ruiz: one more on routing: we use namespace routing within our platform to isolate customers. can Redwood support tenant isolation via Kubernetes namespaces or separate subnets for models?
[06:31] Priya Nair: yes both. software-level tenant isolation is enforced in the runtime, but we also support strict network isolation—per-tenant subnets and security groups. for extreme isolation we can run dedicated model pools per tenant.
[06:43] Anika Bose: and how do you handle KV cache—any cross-tenant leaks?
[06:48] Priya Nair: cache is namespaced per model and per customer; no cross-tenant caching. we also have eviction and TTL controls.
[06:55] Marco Ruiz: excellent. about egress to external SaaS (we call out to enrichment APIs) can we route those via our proxies?
[07:02] Priya Nair: yes you can configure the nodes to use your outbound proxies, or you can have Redwood-managed proxies with whitelisting. for regulatory workloads you should proxy via your infrastructure.
[07:12] Devon Grant: latency and bandwidth for large token outputs—how do you avoid throttling on the egress?
[07:19] Priya Nair: we support streaming responses over HTTP2 gRPC and chunked streaming. bandwidth planning depends on output size and QPS; we'll help estimate egress.
[07:28] Marco Ruiz: any gotchas with on-prem or air-gapped? we might consider an air-gapped npm for very sensitive models.
[07:34] Priya Nair: we have an on-prem package that can be deployed in air-gapped environments, but it requires a separate license and a bit more engineering support. model updates are via physical transfer or signed bundles.
[07:45] Anika Bose: ok that's useful. next, compliance—can we request network flow logs and object-level audit for a 90-day retention?
[07:53] Priya Nair: yes, retention is configurable; we can push logs to your S3/Cloud storage and meet 90-day retention.
[08:00] Liam Chen: let's recap the key constraints: customer-managed infra preferred, APAC residency mandatory for primary processing, KMS/HSM control required, no public egress desirable, need pilot with sub-100ms latency targets for sync endpoints. does that sound right?
[08:12] Marco Ruiz: yes that captures it.
[08:14] Devon Grant: and action on our side is to send CIDRs and TGW IDs.
[08:18] Anika Bose: security will review SOC2 pack and KMS integrations.
[08:22] Priya Nair: action on Redwood: we'll send the private endpoint topology doc, IP planning template, security pack, and proposed pilot checklist.
[08:31] Liam Chen: perfect. any final questions?
[08:33] Marco Ruiz: only one—how quickly can we spin up a pilot if we share CIDRs today?
[08:38] Priya Nair: once we have CIDRs and IAM roles, typically 2-3 weeks to get a customer-managed pilot infra ready; if you want Redwood-managed dedicated capacity it's faster, like 5-7 business days.
[08:49] Marco Ruiz: we'll aim for 2-3 weeks.
[08:52] Liam Chen: great. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the pilot kickoff next week. thanks everyone.
[08:58] Meeting end.
